title: A Spire for the Veil
premise: Quentin Nystrom, a bone-carver who hears the dead through the relics they carve, keeps the ledgers of the Veil—a guild of invisible artisans who trade in impossible things while erasing themselves from every record. When the old gods begin answering prayers again, their returning attention threatens to make the guild visible, and visible things in this country are conscripted, consumed, or killed. Quentin discovers the ledgers hold a hidden map to a door out of a country that officially no longer exists—but opening it requires a sacrifice of memory, and the dead who guide him want it to be his. In the end, Quentin chooses truth over loyalty: he publishes the guild's erased history to the gods themselves, buying passage for his found family at the cost of his own name, which only one person—the ledger-keeper's apprentice—agrees to remember.
about_author: Astrid Dunmore is the pen name of a former archivist who spent a decade cataloguing unclaimed estates and swears half of them whispered back. She writes fantasy about bureaucracy, grief, and the stubborn tenderness of small communities.

chapters.title: The Ledger of Unclaimed Names
chapters.summary: Quentin's POV. We meet the Veil's workshop: bone-carvers, memory-brokers, and Quentin balancing ledgers that record people who officially never existed. A carved knucklebone begins whispering a prayer answered by something old. Emotional beat: quiet unease beneath routine warmth.

chapters.title: What the Gods Remember
chapters.summary: Apprentice Sefa's POV. The first god answers a street child's prayer publicly, and the city celebrates while the Veil panics—divine attention makes the invisible legible. Quentin argues for staying; Sefa argues for running. Emotional beat: the first crack between loyalty and survival.

chapters.title: Bone Whispers
chapters.summary: Quentin's POV. Following the whispering relic, Quentin meets the ghost of the guild's founder, who claims the ledgers contain a door out of the country. The founder warns that gods collect what they can see. Emotional beat: temptation of escape versus duty to those left behind.

chapters.title: The Guild That Wasn't
chapters.summary: Guildmaster Orla's POV. Orla reveals she has been quietly feeding names to the gods to keep them distracted from the rest—an act of protection that looks like betrayal. Quentin confronts her with the founder's map. Emotional beat: loyalty strained by secrets kept 'for our own good.'

chapters.title: A Country Erased
chapters.summary: Sefa's POV. The pair travels into the Hollow Marches, where the nation's official history says nothing exists, guided by dead voices only Quentin hears. They find ruins full of other erased guilds who didn't escape. Emotional beat: dread—erasure is not safety but slow death.

chapters.title: The Price of Passage
chapters.summary: Quentin's POV. At the threshold of the door, the founder's ghost explains the toll: a memory given wholly to the gods, who will then see you forever. Quentin realizes the founder gave her own name centuries ago. Emotional beat: horror reframed as understanding.

chapters.title: Ledger-Burning
chapters.summary: Orla's POV. Back home, the gods' attention turns fully on the Veil; a rival guild sells them out for visibility. Orla burns the false ledgers to hide the true map's location, wounding herself in the guild's memory. Emotional beat: sacrifice as both love and damage.

chapters.title: Truth Before the Gods
chapters.summary: Quentin's POV. Climax. At the door, instead of surrendering a private memory, Quentin reads the guild's entire erased history aloud to the assembled gods—making them witnesses rather than owners. The door opens, but the gods claim his name as payment. Emotional beat: defiant clarity.

chapters.title: Through the Door
chapters.summary: Sefa's POV. The found family crosses into the unnamed land beyond, carrying Orla, wounded but alive. Sefa watches Quentin, now nameless to everyone including himself, still instinctively keeping accounts. Emotional beat: bittersweet arrival, grief braided with relief.

chapters.title: One Person Remembers
chapters.summary: Sefa's POV, closing. In the new country, the guild rebuilds openly. Sefa begins a new ledger whose first entry is Quentin's name, spoken aloud each morning so it cannot be collected again. Somewhere, the dead approve. Emotional beat: resolution—memory kept alive by choice, not magic.
